approved: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a mandatory scheme for car makers and other data holders to sell repair information to Australian mechanics and training providers at a fair price.

Data providers must offer the information, charge no more than fair market value, and supply it promptly after payment, with penalties of up to $10 million for companies and $500,000 for individuals for non-compliance.
Providers must also publish offers online, restrict access to safety and security information, protect personal data, and pay copyright compensation to third parties.
Establishes a mandatory information-sharing scheme for motor vehicle service and repair data.
Imposes obligations on data providers to supply information at fair market value.
Sets maximum penalties of $10 million for body corporates and $500,000 for other persons.
Requires publication of scheme offers and notification to the scheme adviser.
Restricts access to safety and security information to those meeting specified criteria.
Requires compensation to third parties holding copyright in scheme information.

Data providers (including vehicle manufacturers, information owners, licensees, and data aggregators), Australian repairers, and registered training organisations (RTOs) providing vehicle repair training.

The bill establishes a mandatory scheme requiring car manufacturers to sell service and repair information to independent repairers at fair market value, aiming to address a lack of competition in the $23 billion Australian automotive sector. The scheme applies to passenger and light-goods vehicles from 2002, includes a maximum penalty of $10 million for non-compliance, and provides a $250,000 grant for an online information portal.

The speaker argued that the government's delays in implementing a mandatory code for sharing vehicle repair data with independent mechanics have hurt small businesses and consumers, noting Labor first proposed the policy in 2018 after the ACCC's 2017 report. The bill requires manufacturers to supply diagnostic and repair information to all Australian repairers and training organisations at fair market value, with the scheme to take effect on 1 July 2022.

The Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021 was supported to ensure independent repairers have equal access to vehicle service and repair information, creating a level playing field and promoting competition and consumer benefits.

The Labor MP argued that the Morrison government delayed too long in implementing mandatory data-sharing for independent mechanics, which the 2014 voluntary scheme failed to achieve. The bill requires car manufacturers to share service and repair information with independent repairers on fair terms, supporting small businesses, consumer choice, and apprenticeships.

The Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021 aims to end manufacturer monopolies by mandating access to diagnostic and repair information on fair terms, promoting competition and lower prices. The mandatory data sharing scheme will end anticompetitive practices by car manufacturers, lowering costs for households and supporting independent mechanics. The speaker supported the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021 and the second reading amendment, arguing the government had delayed action since 2018 and that Labor’s advocacy—including by the member for Fenner—was essential to finally requiring car manufacturers to share technical information with independent mechanics on fair terms, benefiting 23,000 independent repairers and car owners.

Labor argued for the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021, which would require car manufacturers to share technical information with independent mechanics on fair terms, benefiting over 50 independent repairers in the electorate of Burt and giving car owners more choice.

The Competition and Consumer Amendment (Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Information Sharing Scheme) Bill 2021 mandates that car manufacturers share service and repair data with independent mechanics at a fair price, benefiting 23,000 independent repairers and around 18 businesses in the Oxley electorate. The speaker credited the member for Fenner as a key advocate and noted that the policy, first committed to in 2018, levels the playing field for small operators against large dealerships.

The speaker argued that car manufacturers have withheld intellectual property and diagnostic tools from independent motor mechanics, harming small businesses and inflating repair costs—citing a $800 battery replacement—and supported the bill to drive competition.

The government initiated the motor vehicle service and repair information sharing reforms in 2017, not borrowed from the Labor Party, and the bill establishes a mandatory scheme requiring information to be made available at fair market price—the first of its kind in Australia and the Asia-Pacific region—to promote competition and benefit independent repairers and consumers.
